data.name: Ares
data.gender_notes: Ares is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Ares is the god of war, courage, and strength. He is also known for his violent temper. The name Ares carries the meaning “God of War” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ares usually hope their child will grow to embody god of war and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes courage and strength in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Ares belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of War.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ares total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_latin.name: Ares
in_latin.meaning: God of War, associated with violence and bloodlust in Greek mythology.
in_latin.long_meaning: Ares, in Latin, is a name derived from the Greek mythological figure, associated with war and violence. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, Ares' counterpart, Mars, is often cited in Christian literature as a symbol of strife and conflict. In early Christian tradition, Ares was seen as a representation of the fallen angel Azazel, who led humanity astray. In modern Christian culture, the name Ares is not commonly used and is often associated with pagan mythology.

In Christian tradition, Ares is seen as a representation of the fallen angel Azazel, who led humanity astray. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, Ares' counterpart, Mars, is often cited in Christian literature as a symbol of strife and conflict. In modern Christian culture, the name Ares is not commonly used and is often associated with pagan mythology. Ares is often associated with traits such as aggression, competitiveness, and boldness. In terms of biblical roots, Ares is not directly referenced, but its counterpart, Mars, is mentioned in the Bible as a symbol of war and conflict.

data.cultural_impact: Ares, as the god of war in Greek mythology, stood at the center of martial valor, military expertise, and the courage it takes to engage in battle. He was considered a fierce and belligerent deity, and his cult was practiced mainly in military contexts. Roman soldiers even invoked him as they climbed their standard, the Aquila, before entering battle.
data.spiritual_significance: Metaphorically, Ares represents the raw, human emotions and instincts that fuel the human heart in times of strife, allowing us to confront our fears, fight for what we believe in, and display unwavering courage. This deity's spiritual significance lies in the determination we show against life's adversaries, demonstrating an enduring testimony to our inner fortitude and fierce spirit.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ares, the Christian name for Mars, represents the warrior within us all, our innate strength and will to fight against adversity and sin. It symbolizes courage, determination, and the power to overcome obstacles in our spiritual journey towards God.

biblical_reference.note: Ares is not directly mentioned in the Bible, but its counterpart, Mars, is often cited in Christian literature as a symbol of strife and conflict.

historical_references.reference: Some early Christians identified the Roman god Mars with the Greek god Ares, and equated them with Jesus. This syncretization can be traced back to at least the 3rd century AD.

During the Middle Ages, the Catholic Church promoted the veneration of saints associated with Mars/Ares, such as St. George and St. Demetrius, who were believed to have supernatural martial abilities and protection.

modern_usage.modern_context: The ancient Greek god Ares, known as the god of war, is a popular figure in modern culture. His name is often used in various contexts, particularly in the fields of gaming, mythology, and pop culture. In gaming, Ares is a character or element in several PC games, such as World of Tanks and God of War. In tabletop role-playing games (RPGs), Ares may be a deity that players can interact with or a concept that influences the game's mechanics. In comics, Ares has been depicted in various titles, including 'Wonder Woman' and 'New Gods.' These platforms showcase the enduring appeal of Ares as a powerful and iconic figure in both ancient and modern mythology.

name_in_real_life.story: Grace Ares, a minister in London, United Kingdom, shares that their name Ares meaning "God of War" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
